The home side's xG for leaves a route to one goal, but its scoreless rate and observed under-1.5 scoring evidence argue against a multi-goal home performance. The first-half profile is often scoreless for Le Havre, making a slower opening compatible with the cluster. Home data are current but the current-season sample is only eight league matches.

primary.description: Paris Saint-Germain establish the clearer territorial and chance-creation control, repeatedly test a home defence with a high current-season concession profile, and convert that into a two- or three-goal away result while Le Havre are often held scoreless.

Elversberg's three-match home sample has produced goals in every game, so Mainz's defensive control is not secure; the interaction favours an open away-leaning match rather than a clean directional call.

match_thesis.summary: Mainz's recent chance creation attacks an Elversberg side conceding markedly more xG than it creates; Elversberg retain a plausible home scoring route, producing an open match with a visitor edge.

score_state_cluster.coverage_summary: Open match centred on Mainz scoring twice, with Elversberg contributing in the primary and draw branches.

away.state_summary: Current-season attack is strong on process: 2.30 xG for per match over seven league games, with a positive xG differential. The away-role current-season sample is only three matches but shows 2.76 xG for and 0.75 xG against per match. Recent results trail the underlying process: current-season goals conceded are higher than xG conceded, while the attack remains productive. Mainz's own PPDA is lower than Elversberg's current full-season figure, supporting an active pressing route rather than a passive away setup. Half-time and second-half records show Mainz can score in both phases, but phase evidence remains thin.

home.state_summary: Across seven current league matches Elversberg create 1.61 xG but concede 2.55 xG per match, with 21.14 shots against. Results are less negative than the underlying xG differential, so the current record should not be read as defensive control. Their three home matches have produced 2.67 goals for and 2.33 against per match; this is a direct but very small venue sample. The prior-season home record was materially stronger, making a home scoring response credible but not enough to override current defensive evidence. Elversberg's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half rate in the current sample, leaving a late-game opening route.

competing.description: Elversberg's home scoring route survives and the hosts trade goals with Mainz, yielding an open draw rather than an away win.

primary.description: Mainz turn their current chance creation into repeated chances against Elversberg's exposed defence; Elversberg score once but cannot prevent the away side from taking the open contest.

tail_breaks.description: Mainz's pressing and chance creation suppress Elversberg's scoring route and produce a controlled clean-sheet away win.

away.state_summary: Espanyol's current-season process is negative: chance creation trails concession volume, and their recent results do not reverse that signal. Their own PPDA indicates less intense pressing than Villarreal's current season figure; sustained away control is therefore less well supported. Goals have lagged the recent xG signal, so process supports control more strongly than a large-margin result. Their pressing figure is more intense than Espanyol's, supporting a home-control route. They also have six days since the last match, though their logged 21-day workload is heavier and includes UEFA matches.

competing.description: Villarreal control much of the chance creation but do not convert a second decisive chance; Espanyol's scoring route produces a 1-1 draw.

primary.description: Villarreal generate the greater attacking volume and eventually take control of the score, but Espanyol retain a credible one-goal reply.

tail_breaks.description: An early exchange removes game control and creates a more open home win with four goals.
